schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The abstract ticket class. A ticket is a machine: Ticket.at(fileref) loads its plan and state, queueme(gate) asks the gate's holder over the bus (codemother, verb machines/<gate>/queueme, body {fileref}) to take it, and the gate's own instance calls passed(target) to move the cursor and tell the harbor and the watchers, or failed(lacks) to send it to FIXME and queue it at design.
why: Akien 2026-11-10 (Q#80/Q#81 answers, outline 3.3.1-3.3.4.3 and 9.6): a ticket is a class and a machine, never a device; it crosses a gate by sending its fileref to devices/codemother/0/machines/<gate>/queueme; the gate instantiates it on its own side and that instance processes the pass or fail; on a pass it goes to the next step and alerts the probes watching the gate, on a fail it asks design to queue it, and with no handler it throws a trouble and waits. Self-queuing belongs to the abstract ticket class, so it is written once, here.
role: the ticket's own acts at a gate: ask to be queued, record the dialog, cross on a pass, kick back on a fail
falsifier: A ticket's queueme reaches no gate, or reaches one without its fileref, or a bounce leaves no trouble standing; or passed() moves a cursor without the emit chokepoint, or tells nobody; or failed() leaves the ticket outside FIXME or without its lacks.
owner: codemother (the care of the code, ruling 2026-09-06); CC co-listed until codemother's gate machines (queueme wave T3) are its callers
how_it_learns: It does not; the dialog it logs at each gate (log kind gate_dialog) is the record a gate's learner reads.
state_and_history: No state of its own: every write lands in the ticket's own three files (plan, state, log) through ticket_file and ticket_log, and every crossing in the gate's journal through transitions.emit.
